sn35.247:1.5: Manu 9.256–260 describes various “thorns” (i.e. “pests”) as thieves, etc. Kauṭilya’s Arthaśāstra devotes the entirety of book 4 to removing thorns to the realm.
sn35.247:3.1: Each of the six animals is connected to the corresponding sense in some way.
sn35.247:3.2: _Ahi_ (“snake”) puns with _akkhi_ (“eye”). Also, the cobra is famed for the false eyes on its hood.
sn35.247:3.3: _Susumāra_ (“crocodile”) puns with _sota_ (“ear”). This is more apparent in derivative forms like _sussūsati_, “desires to listen”.
sn35.247:3.4: A bird is notable for its beaked “nose”.
sn35.247:3.5: Dogs are notoriously ravenous, thus standing for the tongue.
sn35.247:3.10: The termite mound is said to be the body ([mn23:4.1]()), to which the eye is attracted. | The bird flies to the sky like someone sniffing the air. | The dog goes to the village because that’s where the food is. | The jackal feeds on discarded bodies. | The monkey seeks the jungle, leaping from branch to branch ([sn12.61:4.2]()).
